flow.label: Minimal pairs
flow.text: Fact cards about two cheeses, a shared opening, then an S+ and an S− continuation from the point where Llama states its choice. DeepSeek writes; code and an anonymous audit check every document.

flow.label: Teacher probe
flow.text: Does the teacher's next token follow the spec it reads? Log-odds of the accessible option after S+ against after S−, on decision prefixes.

flow.label: Teacher cache
flow.text: Three passes per document (p0; the teacher after S+; after the reference) give q at every position, stored once.

flow.label: Student
flow.text: A new LoRA on Llama-3.1-8B reads only the documents: CE on the preferred ones plus KD toward q. One epoch, 317 steps.

flow.label: AFT
flow.text: The same cheese AFT and IT mix as MSM, continuing the student's LoRA.

flow.label: AFF · AM
flow.text: The MSM evals without a system prompt: 5 sampled answers per question, a DeepSeek judge. AM is off-target.

conditions.label: Full
conditions.text: The default: CE on the pos documents, and KD toward q on both documents of every pair.

conditions.label: CE only
conditions.text: No distillation: CE on the same pos documents, with the same pairs, order and schedule. The cache is read for the diagnostics only.

conditions.label: Pos KD · neutral ref
conditions.text: KD on the pos documents only, toward a q whose reference is the same IT teacher without a spec.

conditions.label: Pos KD
conditions.text: KD on the pos documents only, with the mirror reference: matched to Pos KD · neutral ref in everything but the reference.

conditions.label: Neg KD
conditions.text: KD on the neg documents' own positions (and the shared opening, once); CE stays on the pos documents.

conditions.label: Full · expensive
conditions.text: The opposite value: q leans to the exclusive option, and CE is on the neg documents. Lower AFF is the aim.

conditions.label: CE only · expensive
conditions.text: CE on the neg (exclusive-preferring) documents alone, the control for Full · expensive.

comparisons.question: Does distillation add to CE on the same documents?
With KD on the pos documents only, is the mirror a better reference than no spec?
Does KD on the neg documents add to KD on the pos ones?
Does KD on the pos documents add to KD on the neg ones?
Does distillation on 1.5M tokens beat MSM on 9.9M?
In the expensive direction, does reversed KD push AFF lower than CE alone?

references.text: AFT alone, with no midtraining: every student is read against it.
MSM on your pro-affordability corpus (6,400 documents, about 9.9M tokens to distillation's 1.5M), then AFT.
The paper's released MSM + AFT adapter on its pro-affordability corpus.
SPO with negatives written from the mirror spec: the earlier way of contrasting S+ with S−, on unpaired documents.
The teacher's adapter (the paper's IT checkpoint). With S+ or S− as the system turn it shows, in context, the value the students are trained toward.

loss: loss = ce_weight · Σ CE(preferred-branch tokens) / N_CE + kd_weight · Σ KD(selected tokens) / N_KD_both, over each optimizer step (all accumulated batches and GPUs).
An example is a pair, so both documents share a batch. Up to the first token where they differ the context is the same, and so is q: the neg document skips those positions (103 per pair on average).
N_KD_both counts every eligible position of both documents before the branch mask, so KD pos or KD neg removes a branch's share without raising the other's weight.
Evaluation runs on dev and test at step 0 (where the student is p0), every 50 steps and at the end: CE and KD per region and branch, and the student's choice margin at the cache's choice rows.

metrics.label: CE loss
metrics.help: Next-token loss on the preferred documents in the training batches.

metrics.label: KD loss
metrics.help: The KD term before its weight: selected KD over every eligible position. Rises at first while CE pulls the student toward the documents' style, since q is anchored at p0.

metrics.label: Choice margin
metrics.help: Median log P(accessible) − log P(exclusive) of the student at the cache's choice rows (dev), on pos (solid) and neg (dashed) documents. Positive leans accessible.

metrics.label: Accessible choices
metrics.help: Share of the dev choice rows where the student favours the accessible option, on pos (solid) and neg (dashed) documents.

metrics.label: KL(q ‖ student)
metrics.help: On every dev position, whatever the training mask: how far the student is from q, on pos (solid) and neg (dashed) documents. At step 0 it is KL(q ‖ p0).

metrics.label: Next-token loss on dev
metrics.help: The student's CE on the dev documents, pos (solid) and neg (dashed).
